findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan, scale 1" = 20') reveals that electrical meters are mounted directly on the building foundation walls for all eight buildings. Underground electric conduit and lines routing to these meters are shown running immediately adjacent to (and in some cases directly against) the building foundation walls. Specifically: Building 1 meter on northwest corner wall with conduit running along west foundation; Building 2 meter on south wall with branch line routing directly to recessed area; Building 3 meter on east wall with line running to foundation; Building 4 meter on north wall with line from northeast pull box; Building 7 meter on east wall with conduit from southeast corner; Building 8 meter on north wall (recessed notch) with lines routing along foundations. The electrical conduit serving each meter breaches the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone and runs within inches of the building foundations.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires a minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities (duct banks, conduit, pull boxes, manholes) to customer buildings and foundations. The site plan clearly shows electrical meters mounted directly on building walls with underground conduit routed immediately adjacent to building foundations. This is a direct violation of the minimum 5-foot clearance requirement. The presence of wall-mounted meters inherently requires conduit to enter the building within the 5-foot zone. This is not a design that coordinates with the clearance requirement—it fundamentally violates it.
findings.comment: All eight building foundations have underground electric conduit routing within 5 feet (typically within 0 to 2 feet) of building walls to serve wall-mounted electrical meters. This violates the required 5-foot minimum horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to building foundations. Either relocate meters to comply with clearance or coordinate with Austin Energy for exception per UCM § 1.10.5.B.

applicableAreas: Courtyard area between Buildings 4-7, near Building 2, near Buildings 7-8
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) and cross-reference with Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) reveals multiple storm drain inlets positioned directly adjacent to or within close proximity of underground electrical infrastructure. Specific conflicts identified: (1) Central courtyard area contains four 18" grate inlets (Rim elevations 683.13, 683.15, 682.95, 683.10) positioned in the central landscaped/hardscape courtyard where transformer pads are located; (2) West of Building 2, an 18" grate inlet (Rim 683.82) is positioned directly adjacent to the "E" (electrical) utility line running along the western boundary; (3) South of Buildings 7 and 8, a series of 2'x2' grate inlets (Rims 679.30, 679.94, 680.99) are located in the drive aisle directly in proximity to electrical infrastructure serving those buildings. These drain inlets are located within the 5-foot horizontal clearance zone required between underground electric facilities and other site improvements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires minimum 5 feet horizontal clearance from underground electric facilities to site improvements and hardscape features. Storm drain inlets are site drainage improvements that require clearance from electrical infrastructure. The courtyard inlets appear to be directly adjacent to or within the transformer pad areas, and the Building 2 inlet is positioned directly on the electrical line corridor. Visual analysis at the 1" = 20' scale indicates these inlets fall within 5 feet (and likely within 0-3 feet) of the electrical conduit and transformer pads. This represents a coordination failure between drainage design and electrical routing.
findings.comment: Multiple storm drain inlets are proposed within 5 feet of underground electric facilities. Specifically, courtyard inlets conflict with transformer pads, and the inlet west of Building 2 is positioned directly adjacent to the electrical utility line. Revise drain inlet locations to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all underground electric facilities, or coordinate with Austin Energy for encasement/protection measures if clearance cannot be achieved.

findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) reveals electrical pull boxes positioned in close proximity to building foundations at multiple locations: (1) Building 1: Pull box at southwest corner, appearing to be within 5 feet (visually estimated 2-4 feet) of the corner; (2) Building 4: Pull box to the northeast near Unit 404, positioned close to the east foundation line, appearing to be at or near the 5-foot threshold; (3) Building 7: Pull box at southeast corner near Unit 704, appearing to be within 5 feet of the corner; (4) Building 8: Pull box at northwest corner near Unit 801, appearing to be within 5 feet of the corner. These pull boxes are shown as discrete symbols positioned immediately adjacent to building corners rather than at clear standoff distances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.B requires pull boxes to maintain 5 feet clearance from all sides, including from building foundations and property lines. Pull boxes are underground electrical facilities that must be accessible for maintenance, and the code establishes clearance from structures to ensure they are not impacted by building foundations or other improvements. The visual positioning of pull boxes at or within building corners (at the 1" = 20' scale) indicates they fail to maintain the required 5-foot clearance zone around them. This is particularly problematic because pull boxes require working space for access and maintenance.
findings.comment: Four electrical pull boxes (near Buildings 1, 4, 7, and 8) are positioned within 5 feet of building foundations and corners. Relocate pull boxes to maintain 5-foot minimum clearance from all sides per UCM § 1.10.5.B, or provide justification if clearance maintenance is infeasible and coordinate with Austin Energy Design.

applicableAreas: Central area between Buildings 7-8, between Buildings 2-3, south of Building 7
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 12 (Storm Sewer Plan) identifies three storm drain manholes with locations that conflict with pedestrian and vehicular site features: (1) SD Manhole between Buildings 2 and 3 (Rim 684.71): Located in a landscaped/pedestrian area directly adjacent to a north-south sidewalk routing, creating a maintenance access conflict and potential trip hazard in a pedestrian circulation path; (2) SD Manhole between Buildings 7 and 8 (Rim 683.78): Located in a paved pedestrian sidewalk threshold connecting the southern parking area to the central courtyard, directly in a pedestrian travel path; (3) SD Manhole south of Building 7 (Rim 681.02): Located directly in the paved vehicle driveway path, a primary vehicle circulation area. These manhole locations overlap with primary site circulation routes rather than being positioned in dedicated utility access areas.
findings.reasoning: Manhole placement must not conflict with site features that require vertical transitions (stairs, ramps, accessible routes) and should not be located directly in high-traffic pedestrian or vehicular circulation paths. The three manholes are positioned in: one in a pedestrian sidewalk area, one directly in a pedestrian pathway serving multiple buildings, and one in a primary vehicle driveway. These locations create conflicts with site circulation, accessibility, maintenance access, and pose potential trip hazards. Manhole covers in circulation paths are a code compliance issue and accessibility/safety concern.
findings.comment: Three storm drain manholes are located directly in pedestrian sidewalk areas and vehicle driveway paths. Relocate manholes to utility easement areas outside of primary circulation routes, or modify site plan to accommodate manhole access without creating conflicts with pedestrian routes, ramps, or vehicle drives.

applicableAreas: Central drive aisle, west entrance area, north perimeter, south perimeter

findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) confirms that underground electric conduit (shown as blue "E" lines on Sheet 21) crosses water lines (shown as "W" lines) at multiple locations: (1) West entrance/valley view road area; (2) Central drive aisle (multiple crossings); (3) North perimeter near Buildings 1-3; (4) South perimeter. However, no utility profile sheets or detail sections are provided that specifically show the vertical clearance or horizontal separation distances at these crossing points. Sheet 20 (Utility Tap Profile) shows water line profiles but does not address electric/water line crossings. No detail sheets specify whether concrete encasement, sleeves, or other protection measures are provided at crossing points.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal and vertical clearance between electric conduit and water lines when crossing perpendicularly. While the site plan clearly shows electric and water lines crossing at multiple locations, the provided plans do not include profile details, vertical clearance dimensions, or crossing detail sections that would allow verification of compliance with the 12-inch minimum clearance requirement. Without profile sheets or crossing detail specifications, it cannot be determined from the available evidence whether the required clearances are maintained or whether any utility coordination/encasement is specified.
findings.comment: Electric conduit and proposed water lines cross at multiple locations on the site (central drive aisle, north/south perimeters). Provide utility profile sheets or crossing detail sections for all electric/water line intersections showing minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical separation, or specify concrete encasement and protection measures at crossing points per UCM § 1.10.5.A.

applicableAreas: Central drive aisle, north perimeter, south perimeter, courtyard area
findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) confirms that underground electric conduit (blue "E" lines) crosses wastewater lines ("WW" lines) at multiple locations: (1) Central drive aisle (multiple north-south crossings); (2) North perimeter; (3) Courtyard area (multiple branch lines); (4) South perimeter. However, no utility profile sheets or crossing detail sections are provided that specify vertical clearance distances or horizontal separation at these crossing points. Sheet 19 specifies wastewater branch material (6" PVC at 2.0% minimum slope) but does not address electric/wastewater crossing clearances or protection measures.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 12 inches (1 foot) horizontal and vertical clearance between electric conduit and wastewater lines when crossing perpendicularly. The site plan shows electric and wastewater lines crossing at multiple locations, but the provided documentation does not include profile sheets, crossing detail sections, or clearance specifications that would verify compliance with the 12-inch minimum requirement. Without crossing profiles or details, the vertical and horizontal separations at crossing points cannot be verified from the available evidence.
findings.comment: Electric conduit and proposed wastewater lines cross at multiple locations (central drive aisle, courtyard, perimeters). Provide utility profile sheets or crossing detail sections showing minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical separation at all electric/wastewater intersections, or specify concrete encasement and protection measures per UCM § 1.10.5.A.

applicableAreas: Central drive aisle, north perimeter, courtyard
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) and Sheet 19 (Utility Tap Plan) show that underground electric facilities and both water and wastewater lines are present and will cross at multiple locations on site. However, no utility profile sheets or vertical clearance detail sections are provided. Sheet 20 shows water line profile (Water Line A) with flowline elevations but does not show electric line elevations or vertical separation at crossing points. Without cross-sectional details or profile views showing the vertical relationship between electric and water/wastewater utilities at crossing points, vertical clearances cannot be verified.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.5.A requires minimum 1 foot (12 inches) vertical clearance from underground electric facilities to water and wastewater lines at crossing points. While the plans confirm that these utilities cross, the provided documentation does not include utility profile sheets showing the vertical elevation relationships at crossing locations. This is essential information to verify compliance. The absence of crossing profiles makes it impossible to confirm that minimum vertical clearances are maintained from the available evidence.
findings.comment: Utility profile sheets or crossing detail sections must be provided for all locations where proposed water and wastewater lines cross underground electric facilities, showing minimum 12-inch vertical clearance and confirming which utility is positioned above the other. Provide elevation data and crossing detail sections per UCM § 1.10.5.A.

findings.observation: Visual analysis of Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows that underground electric conduit is routed to and directly beneath building foundations to serve electrical meters mounted on building walls. Specifically: (1) All eight buildings have underground electric lines routing to wall-mounted meters; (2) These lines originate from transformers or pull boxes and run directly to the building serving as conduit entry points; (3) The conduit must pass beneath or immediately adjacent to building foundations to reach the meters; (4) In some cases (Buildings 2, 8), the meters are mounted in recessed notches in the building walls, requiring conduit to route into these recessed areas. This represents a direct routing of underground electric facilities beneath building foundations and service areas.
findings.reasoning: Wall-mounted electrical meters inherently require underground conduit to be routed to the building. When buildings are designed with slab-on-grade construction (as noted in the site data), conduit routing beneath the slab violates the prohibition. While some conduit may pass through retaining walls below grade (with an exception per UCM § 1.10.5.B requiring license agreement and engineering), the routing of conduit as the primary service to wall-mounted meters is not addressed by this exception.
findings.comment: Underground electric conduit routing to serve wall-mounted electrical meters on all eight buildings would require conduit to pass beneath or through building foundations, which violates UCM § 1.10.5.B. Relocate electrical meters to pedestals or external equipment enclosures outside of building footprints, or coordinate with Austin Energy Design to document a license agreement and sealed engineering design if conduit must pass through building foundations, with metal sleeves allowing replacement.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meters are mounted directly on building foundation walls for all eight buildings. However, the plan does not provide sufficient detail regarding the specific mounting locations relative to building architectural features. Visual positioning suggests meters are mounted on exterior sidewalls, but the plans do not explicitly indicate: (1) Whether any meters are located under porches, covered entryways, or overhangs; (2) The exact relationship to stairways (some buildings have units with stairs); (3) Whether any meters are located under carports or covered parking areas; (4) The relationship to accessible routes or ramps. Sheet 21 notation indicates building FFEs and unit numbers but does not detail these specific meter location constraints.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 prohibits electric meters from being located on/under porches, stairways, under overhangs exceeding 72 inches, carports, or where moving objects might damage equipment. The site plan shows meters are wall-mounted but does not provide the architectural detail necessary to confirm they are not located under prohibited features. Meters appear to be on building sides, but without building elevation drawings or detail sections showing the relationship of meters to overhangs, carports, and architectural features, compliance cannot be verified.
findings.comment: Building elevations or meter location detail sheets must be provided showing that electrical meters are NOT located on/under porches, stairways, overhangs exceeding 72 inches, carports, or other prohibited locations per UCM § 1.9.3.1. Provide building elevations with meter locations clearly identified relative to architectural features.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows three transformer pads located on the property: (1) One west of Building 2; (2) One west of Building 8; (3) One centrally located in the courtyard between Buildings 4-7. Electrical meters are mounted on building walls for all eight buildings. However, the site plan does not provide line-of-sight verification or dimensional data showing the relationship between meter locations and transformer locations. Without building elevation drawings, it cannot be confirmed whether meters are on first floor/ground level relative to their respective serving transformers or whether sight lines between meters and transformers are maintained (unobstructed by buildings, walls, or other features).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires electrical meters to be located on first floor or ground level and within sight of the serving AE transformer. While the plan shows meters and transformers, it does not provide the elevation information (first floor vs. upper floors) or line-of-sight verification necessary to confirm compliance. Meters on a multi-story townhome building could potentially be on upper floors, and sight lines could be obstructed by other buildings or structures.
findings.comment: Provide building elevations and a site plan diagram showing sight lines between all electrical meters and their serving transformers, confirming that: (1) meters are located on first floor or ground level, and (2) unobstructed sight line exists from transformer to meter per UCM § 1.9.3.1.

findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical meter locations but does not show or reference electrical service disconnect switch locations. The electrical design plan does not identify where main disconnect switches or service disconnects are located relative to meters. Without this information, the distance between meters and disconnects cannot be verified from the available site plan documentation.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.9.3.1 requires that the distance between electric meter and disconnect does not exceed 20 feet, and meter and disconnect must be within line of sight. The site plan does not show disconnect switch locations, making it impossible to verify this requirement from the available evidence. Building electrical plans or riser diagrams that show disconnect switch locations would be necessary to make this determination.
findings.comment: Provide building electrical plans, riser diagrams, or service disconnect location drawings showing the distance between electrical meters and their serving main service disconnects, confirming distance does not exceed 20 feet and that meter and disconnect are within line of sight per UCM § 1.9.3.1.
